newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Shilling stable on dollar, gains on pound.
newsitem.headline: Shilling stable on dollar, gains on pound.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling finished the week on Friday unchanged against the dollar and up on the pound, the central bank said.
Against the dollar, the shilling exchanged at a mean rate of 598.0689, while against the pound the local currency exchanged at 963.7911 compared to Thursday's mean of 972.1640.
Dealers told Reuters the shilling had depreciated slightly during the week but there was no cause for alarm.
"The T-shilling depreciated slightly -- that's because NBC (state-owned National Bank of Commerce) has not been in the market regularly," said one dealer.
Asked if the depreciation was raising alarm bells, the dealer replied: "I don't think so -- I have no problems with the level."
The dealer, who asked not to be named, said the NBC had been active the market only three times this week compared to daily presence prior to January 24.

"The determining factors that affect the exchange rate are intervention by either NBC or the Bank of Tanzania (BoT,") said the dealer. A second financial analyst agreed, saying the absence of the NBC from the market followed the governments decision to divide the bank into the three components.
"Now the (NBC) management is reacting to new strategies following the split -- they're in a holding pattern and in shock," said the analyst.
The second analyst said the shilling would continue to depreciate slightly for the next month following a surge of imports to replenish stocks depleted over the Christmas, New Year holiday period.
"Despite the slight depreciation, the shilling is fundamentally strong," he told Reuters.
"It would be strange if it got much weaker because the market here is driven by the budget and the budget is improving," he said.
Last Friday the shilling exchanged at a commercial mean rate of 597.7620 against the dollar.
